body:
## Summary

A server that was stopped on purpose comes straight back if a client has that host as an **enabled saved SSH machine**. On its next reconnect attempt, the client's `remote-client-bridge` finds nothing listening and spawns a new `herdr server`. That happens whatever command stopped the server: `herdr server stop`, `herdr session stop <name>`, or the service manager (`launchctl kill TERM`). There is currently no way to say "attach only, never start".

The docs say the opposite. [Connecting machines](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/blob/v0.9.1/docs/next/website/src/content/docs/connecting-machines.mdx) states that "Background connections never answer prompts or install, update, restart, or hand off a server."

## Environment

- herdr 0.9.1 on the client (macOS arm64) and on both servers (macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64).
- Named session `crystal` on each server, started by the OS service manager (launchd, systemd user unit).
- Client: `herdr machine add <host> --label <host> --remote-session crystal`, then a local client attached.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On host A, start a named-session server: `HERDR_SESSION=crystal herdr server`.
2. On the client, run `herdr machine add A --label A --remote-session crystal`, then open `herdr`. A shows up in the sidebar.
3. On host A, run `HERDR_SESSION=crystal herdr server stop`, or `herdr session stop crystal`.
4. On host A, run `ps -A -o pid,ppid,command | grep herdr` for a few seconds.

**Observed:** about 2 s later, `herdr --session crystal remote-client-bridge --idle-timeout-v1` is running over SSH, together with a new `herdr server` that is its child. The server restores the saved layout as fresh shells.

**Same steps with the machine disabled** (`herdr machine disable <id>`): the stop sticks.

## Where it happens (v0.9.1)

- `src/remote/host.rs:38-60`: `ensure_remote_server_running()` calls `spawn_server_daemon()` whenever nothing is listening.
- `src/client/endpoint/supervisor.rs:281`: every saved-machine connect attempt goes through `connect_saved_ssh`. It retries with a 500 ms initial delay and a 120 s cap (`:11-12`).
- `src/session.rs:260-269`: `session stop` / `server stop` only send `server.stop`. No record is left saying the stop was intentional.

## Why it matters

We run long-lived coding agents in panes of a named session. A server stop kills every pane process, and a restart restores the layout as bare shells that look like the agents' panes. So for us, only the operator may start or restart that server, after a deliberate stop or a reboot. A background client connection silently undoes the stop. The restarted server also inherits the SSH login environment instead of the service unit's.

## Possible directions (any of these would solve it for us)

1. **Honour an explicit stop.** `server stop` / `session stop` records a stopped state. Background and bridge connections do not spawn a server while that state is present; only an interactive `herdr`, `herdr --remote` or `machine add` clears it and starts one.
2. **Attach-only saved machines.** A per-profile option, or a `[remote]` config key, under which the bridge reports "server not running" (Attention) instead of spawning.
3. At minimum, correct the docs sentence above.

Happy to test a build.

comments.body:
Hitting this on 0.9.3 as well (macOS arm64, three Macs, each one a saved machine on the other two).

Same mechanism: after `herdr server stop` on one host, a peer's `remote-client-bridge` spawned a replacement server about a second later, before I could start it locally. On macOS there's a further side effect beyond losing the panes. The respawned server inherits the SSH login's security session, so every pane loses login-keychain access: `gh` and other keychain-backed CLIs fail, and `security show-keychain-info` reports "User interaction is not allowed". The guidance from #966 is to start the server from a GUI terminal, but while peers are connected that start can't win the race. Every stop or reboot is picked up by a peer first.

In a mesh, disabling one client doesn't avoid it, because every machine is a client of the others. The only workaround I have is `herdr machine disable` on every peer before each restart, then re-enabling afterwards.

Either proposed direction would fix it for me. An attach-only `[remote]` config key (direction 2) would be the simplest, since it would cover all saved machines at once. The behavior is still present on master as of c4653a4f (`src/remote/host.rs`, `ensure_remote_server_running()`).

Same thing on Windows, herdr 0.9.4 stable (Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Win32-OpenSSH 10.0p2 server with key-only auth, two Windows machines, each a saved machine on the other).

The trigger is a server restart. Here it was the stop that `herdr update` asks for. The peer's `remote-client-bridge` starts a replacement server before a local start can. On Windows the replacement runs in session 0, its parent is `WmiPrvSE.exe`, and it holds the SSH login's NETWORK token at High integrity. Every pane inherits that token. Windows Credential Manager is out of reach from it, so Git Credential Manager and `gh` both fail in every pane:

```
> whoami /groups   (excerpt, inside a pane)
NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK
Mandatory Label\High Mandatory Level

> git fetch origin
fatal: Unable to persist credentials with the 'wincredman' credential store.
See https://aka.ms/gcm/credstores for more information.
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled

> gh auth status
  X Failed to log in to github.com account <user> (default)
  - The token in default is invalid.

> cmdkey /list   -> 0 entries (10 from the desktop session)
```

The token is fine. It reads as invalid only because the keyring can't be reached.

The race is easy to lose, the same as on macOS. In one attempt I ran `herdr server stop` at the console, and the bridge had a new server up before the local start. I start the server from a logon scheduled task (interactive, Medium). That run came 36 s later and its `herdr server` exited with code 1. The local start won only after I fully quit the peer's herdr client first. With the server started from the desktop session, the pane shows `NT AUTHORITY\INTERACTIVE`, Medium integrity, `cmdkey` lists 10 entries, and `git fetch` and `gh` work. Reattaching from the peer afterwards is fine.

A smaller Windows side effect: a Medium `herdr status server` on the desktop doesn't report the SSH-started (elevated) server as running. A local start script that checks status first therefore doesn't see it.

An attach-only option would fix this for me too.

Still reproducible on 0.9.5 (macOS 27 arm64, client and server both 0.9.5, server run by a user LaunchAgent in the `gui/<uid>` domain).

A consequence specific to macOS that may help prioritise this: the replacement server inherits the environment of the client's non-interactive SSH session, not the GUI session. Agents running in its panes then cannot read the login keychain, so anything that relies on it breaks quietly. For us, Claude Code sessions in those panes lost their Remote Control connection after a routine `launchctl kickstart -k` of the server, because the peer's bridge got there first during the restart gap.

From reading the source, #5236 (spawning through a one-shot GUI launchd job) does not cover this path: `launchd_spawn.rs` falls back to a direct spawn when `SSH_CONNECTION` is set, which is always the case when the bridge starts it.

Workaround we use for now:

1. Before restarting the server on purpose, run `herdr machine disable <host>` on every client that has it saved, restart, wait until the server pid equals the launchd job pid, then `herdr machine enable <host>`.
2. On the server host, a watchdog that looks for a `herdr server` process whose pid is not the LaunchAgent's pid. If it is still there on two checks in a row and no agent is busy, it is sent TERM and the LaunchAgent is kickstarted.

An "attach only, never start" option on saved machines (or making background bridges honour the documented behaviour) would remove the need for both.

Same problem here on Linux, herdr 0.9.5. I would like to add a use case the thread does not have yet: the server is not just stopped on purpose, it has to be started in a specific way, and the bridge's replacement runs in the wrong one.

In my situation, I start the herdr server inside a docker container with certain environment variables set. Connecting to this already-running server works great. But if it's not running, having herdr automatically SSH in and restart a server puts it into the wrong environment. So I also need an attach-only mode or something like "machine add --no-autostart".

Thanks for considering.

So I've been thinking about this a bit and one possible option could be that we track manual shut downs.

Then any client can say "ya no but I WANT this thing to start again right NOW" -> manual start -> other clients auto-attach.

This is potentially a bit tricky with other clients that didn't actively get the shut down notice.

Only issue, as usual, is Windows Session 0 vs 1 annoyances.

Another consequence of the bridge auto-starting the server, linking #966. On macOS, two machines each have the other saved as a remote. After one reboots, the other's `remote-client-bridge` reconnects over SSH within seconds and starts `herdr server` inside the no-tty `sshd-session`. Every pane then inherits a `Background` launchd context (`launchctl managername` → `Background`), and keychain writes pop "A keychain cannot be found… Reset To Defaults".

A per-user `gui/$UID` LaunchAgent, the #966 workaround, only helps if it wins the race. SSH comes up before GUI login, so the bridge usually wins. An attach-only option for saved machines, as this issue asks, would close it: the remote client waits for the GUI-launched server instead of starting its own.

herdr 0.9.3, macOS arm64, both hosts.

same here on 0.9.5, macOS. a mac mini reboots nightly around 04:10 and two peers have it as a saved machine; their bridges win the start race, the server comes up inside sshd, and every Claude Code pane in it is signed out since it can't read the login keychain.

our workaround until there's an attach-only option, in case it helps anyone: an ssh forced command on the peers' keys that passes every command through but refuses `herdr remote-client-bridge` unless a server is already listening on the socket and its environment has no SSH_CONNECTION. the peers just show the box as unreachable until the GUI login starts herdr, then attach on their own.

+1 for an attach-only flag on the saved machine or a server-side "never start from a remote client" setting.
